answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks via optical time-of-flight triangulation. Each node functions as a spatial vertex, timing laser pulses sent to a calibrated optical lantern. Forging identities forces an attacker to deploy discrete physical transceivers across separate coordinates, such as rural ground stations ringed by yarrow, eliminating cost-free virtualization. However, atmospheric fog can scatter line-of-sight beams, occasionally causing false rejections of honest nodes.
